chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Muhammad ibn Sinan from Mu'adh ibn Kathir said:

I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'Leeway is given to our Shias to spend from what is in their hands in a good manner. So when our Qaim rises, it will be prohibited for every owner of a treasure to hoard his treasure until he brings it to him, so that he may use it to assist against his enemy.'
And this is the Word of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic: 'And those who hoard gold and silver and spend it not in the way of Allah, give them tidings of a painful punishment.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on hoarding wealth before and after the rise of the Qaim?
ai.summary: This hadith delineates the economic jurisprudence of the Minor Occultation, where wealth accumulation is permissible, contrasting it with the Major Occultation or the era of the Qaim, where hoarded treasure (kanz) becomes a communal resource for jihad. It explicitly links the prohibition of hoarding to the eschatological role of the Imam, who will utilize these reserves to defeat his enemies, thereby transforming private wealth into a tool for divine victory. This reflects the Shia scholarly view that the Imam’s authority extends to reclaiming stored wealth for the benefit of the community and the establishment of justice.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Muhammad Bin Sinan, from Muaz Bin Kaseer who said,

‘I heard Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> saying: ‘There is leeway upon our<sup>asws</sup> Shias that they can spend from what is in their hands with the acts of kindness. So when our<sup>asws</sup> Qaim<sup>asws</sup> rises, it would be Prohibited unto every one with a treasure to hoard it until he comes with it, so he assists with it against his<sup>asws</sup> enemies,
and these are the Words of Allahazwj Mighty and Majestic [9:34] and (as for) those who hoard up the gold and the silver and do not spend it in Allah's Way, announce to them a painful Punishment’.
en.sarwar: 4. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Muhammad ibn Sinan from Mu’adh ibn Kathir who has said the following: “I heard abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, say, Tt is permissible for our followers to spend as Benevolent Assistance from whatever they possess. When the one with Divine Authority will rise, it will then become unlawful for all possessors of treasure not to bring it to him so he can use it to overcome his enemies.

This is stated in the words of Allah, the Most Majestic, the Most Glorious, ‘Those who treasure gold and silver and do not spend them for the cause of Allah, inform them of the painful torment that awaits them.’”
